ground_truth: When a user sells the entire remaining supply of a token, the exit contribution fee taken by the contract becomes permanently stuck because there is no remaining supply to redeem it against[cite: 2275].

A precision mismatch in the `mintFromExpansion()` function causes the token price to change after execution, violating a core protocol invariant. The amount to mint is calculated with a high-precision ratio, but the updated ratio is stored at a lower precision .

An attacker can front-run expansion functions by buying all G$ tokens to make the supply zero. This causes the controller to add funds to the reserve but mint no new tokens, as the underlying minting function returns 0 when supply is 0, trapping the reserve funds.

The `update()` function uses integer division which rounds down traded amounts, allowing users to bypass trading limits. The function only corrects for rounding if the result is zero, which can be exploited to trade up to double the intended amount through a series of small transactions.

The calculation for the number of expansion periods uses integer division, which always rounds down. This causes the protocol to expand more slowly than designed, as fractions of an expansion period are consistently ignored, leading to fewer tokens being minted over time [cite: 2483-2484, 2500].
